content:
alex: quick design sync: i'm prototyping an 'elastic-lane demux' for continuous batching. goal: keep small, latency-sensitive requests out of bulky-cohort queues without duplicating admission logic. high-level: a lightweight demux that classifies requests into transient lanes and routes to slot pools.
priya: how is this different from our micro-lane idea? feels similar to earlier proposals.
tom: difference: demux is pluggable and stateless; it uses probabilistic steering + deadline hints rather than hard partitioning. cheaper to run and can be toggled per-service.
rachel: i'm worried about consistency with KV cache locality. steering could reduce cache hits and cost us more tokens. any mitigations?
alex: plan A: prefer steering only on cold requests (no kv-tag) and on requests with explicit short_deadline flag. Plan B fallback: keep original slab affinity and perform best-effort prewarm on destination slab when we steer.
priya: what's the API surface? we need a minimal handshake for downstream adapters.
tom: proto idea:

```
request.headers: {
  X-Steer-Tag: "elastic.v1" // optional
  X-Deadline-Hint: "50ms"
}

demux.response: {
  lane: "transient" | "cohort" | "probe",
  steer_reason: "deadline" | "load_skew" | "probing",
  prewarm_token: "bool"
}
```

rachel: telemetry needs: steer_count, steer_reject_count, steer_kv_miss_delta, per-lane p99. also sample traces where steer_reason=probing.
ops-bot: perf-bot: please file a canary checklist before rollout: include steady-state + burst traces.
alex: rollout plan: shadow mode for ~48h, then staggered opt-in by route (percent=5, 20, 100). safety: auto-disable if steer_kv_miss_delta > 0.15 or lane_p99 increases >15% for 5m.
priya: one tradeoff we must document: latency isolation vs. packing efficiency. transient lanes reduce p99 but hurts batching efficiency on coalesced workloads. include cost delta estimate in PR.
tom: implementation note: demux will expose a small control plane metric: estimated_batch_fill_loss. that helps quantify packing loss.
rachel: what about fairness? tenants can't starve because we steer their small requests out. need tenant-weight aware steering.
alex: agreed. steering policy will accept tenant_weight and not exceed fair_share_shift_per_min. config example:

```
elastic_demux {
  enabled: true
  probe_fraction: 0.01
  max_steer_per_tenant_per_min: 10
  deadline_threshold_ms: 80
}
```

priya: can we run a backwards-compatible shim so adapters that expect slab ids still see them?
tom: yes — demux adds a stable_mapped_slab header even when steering; adapters can read allow_steer flag per-route.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: snapshot created for branch elastic-demux/rc1. CI green.
alex: i'll push RFC follow-up doc with perf sims and tradeoff matrix. please annotate with any other corner cases (seqid reorder, optimistic prewarm costs).
rachel: i'll own the observability dashboard. will add cross-lane trace filters. :+1:
priya: i'll review the demux proto and validate adapter compatibility.
tom: thanks all, aiming to land shadow canary tomorrow morning. ping me for infra keys.
